extracted.intended_audience: OEIS users and potential contributors (mathematicians, researchers, hobbyists who use or submit integer sequences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for using the OEIS and for contributing a new integer sequence or updates to existing sequences (what to include, submission prerequisites, how entries are organised and viewed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of a sequence for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Of course the sequence should be well-defined, of general interest and ideally it should be infinite. Short sequences such as phone numbers are not appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only sequences that are well-defined and of general mathematical interest; avoid trivial or purely personal short lists (e.g. phone numbers). The page explicitly discourages short sequences and recommends that sequences be ideally infinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration required before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a new sequence, you must first register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must create an account / register on the OEIS site before they may propose a new sequence or comment. (Separately, the wiki login is different from the OEIS database login.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A group of about 130 editors has been formed, whose job it is to review submissions before they become a permanent part of the OEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are not instantly permanent: they are reviewed by volunteer editors. Expect editorial scrutiny and possible requests or delays before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical contents/fields of an OEIS entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The entry for each sequence gives some or all of: the beginning of the sequence its name or description a graph of the sequence additional comments the offset (index of first term) references or links formulas computer programs cross-references to other sequences the sequence converted to music the name of the person who submitted it the history of the OEIS entry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a submission, include as many of these sections as possible (initial terms, clear description, offset, references, formulas, code, cross-references, submitter name, history/comments). The more complete an entry, the more useful it is. There is also an internal format and a 'text' view where each line is prefixed by a symbol indicating its function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry view / reply formats and what they do
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence pages have little buttons at the top marked 'list', 'graph', 'refs', 'listen', 'history', 'text', 'internal format', and sometimes 'table' and 'edit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'list' produces a numbered list of the terms plus a bracketed list for importing; 'refs' shows sequences which reference this one; 'table' gives 2D views for triangular/table-like sequences; 'graph' produces plots (pin plot of first 200 terms and a linear/log scatter-plot including b-file terms); 'listen' produces a midi file (browser popups may be required); 'history' shows change history; 'edit' appears only for registered users; 'text' shows sections with prefix symbols; 'internal format' shows internal record sections. Use these views to prepare and check your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement / indexing rule for sequences in the database
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences in the OEIS are arranged in lexicographic order, indexed by the position of the first term that is greater than 1 in absolute value. Sequences that contain only 0's, 1's and -1's are in lexicographic order by absolute value at the beginning of the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines where a new sequence will appear and is useful when searching: lexicographic placement gives an essentially unique place to look. Use 'Sequence in context' and 'Adjacent sequences' links to see surrounding entries when uncertain about placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get help identifying a sequence (Superseeker)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have stumped the database, you can try Superseeker, which tries really hard to identify a sequence. Send an empty email message to [email protected] to get instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Superseeker for difficult identification problems; follow the email-instruction mechanism described to access it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to find sequences needing more terms / help
rubrics_metrics.description: See the web page 'Sequences that need more terms' Or use the WebCam to browse the sequences that need more terms Or use the main look-up page to search for the keyword 'more'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to contribute by computing terms, use those pages/tools to find candidate sequences that require additional data. The WebCam can also show sequences flagged as needing more terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting contributors (email privacy policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the current OEIS Wiki, however, email addresses are not made public and a different mechanism is used for contacting contributors. First, find the author in the list of Registered Users and go to the author's User Page. (Make sure you are logged in to the OEIS Wiki - this is different from logging in to the OEIS database). There you will see a button in the left panel saying 'Email this user'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect to find raw email addresses on sequence pages; use the registered-user 'Email this user' facility on the wiki to contact contributors. Be logged into the wiki when using this mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to reference the OEIS or a particular sequence in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have found the OEIS useful and wish to reference it, the usual citation is OEIS Foundation Inc. (2026), The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences, Published electronically at https://oeis.org. Referencing a particular sequence: the URL for sequence A000108 (for example) is https://oeis.org/A000108. A text reference might say: The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences, published electronically at https://oeis.org, 2010, Sequence A000108; or a citation pointing to the A-number and OEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing the OEIS in papers, include the OEIS Foundation citation and, for specific sequences, include the A-number and the sequence URL. The page provides example citation text and URL formats to copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and copyright notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This database and its associated files are copyright 2026 by The OEIS Foundation Inc. Content is available under The OEIS End-User License Agreement unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OEIS content according to the End-User License Agreement; attribute appropriately and be aware of copyright ownership by The OEIS Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal format / text-format conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'text' shows the various sections of the entry for this sequence with each line prefixed by a symbol that indicates its function.'Internal format' shows the various sections of the entry for this sequence in the internal format. For information about the format of replies received from the database, click here. See also the hints file for further useful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn and follow the internal/text prefixes and the internal record format when composing or editing submissions; consult the linked format page and hints file for exact syntax and conventions.
